## Description

Retire `ORPHANED.md` throughout BRM so orphaning and adoption only require changing the `owners` array in a module family's root `metadata.json`.

**Rebased on 2026-09-23:** main `285fc7d0772503382cf5de3e7979d41a12a6e2c1`, new head `6484efc6f86a9d0aaeccd7c065862264150ab333`. The rebase completed without conflicts. Upstream already removed the obsolete orphan-marker compliance assertion in [#7389](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/7389), so that duplicate deletion drops out of this diff. The remaining retirement changes are byte-for-byte identical to the original head; the rebased diff contains 54 files. Upstream metadata-driven reviewer routing from [#7378](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/7378), CSV removal, and governance changes are preserved exactly.

The old compliance assertion compared marker files with owner handles downloaded from the public module index. That index can lag an approved metadata change, as demonstrated by the [network-connection validation failure](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/35779729598/job/106922710486). Ownership validity remains enforced by the shared standalone metadata gate; the retired assertion is not reintroduced or duplicated.

| # | File | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `utilities\pipelines\sharedScripts\Get-ModuleList.ps1` | Resolve ownership from validated root metadata, including inherited child/grandchild ownership and team handles. Cache each root only within the current invocation; surface missing or invalid metadata explicitly. |
| 2 | `utilities\pipelines\sharedScripts\Set-ModuleReadMe.ps1` | Stop reading or inserting orphan markers; retain deprecation and moved-module notices. |
| 3 | `avm\**\ORPHANED.md` | Delete all 25 tracked markers, including the empty dev-center/project marker. |
| 4 | `avm\**\README.md` | Remove exactly the obsolete five-line notice from 24 affected READMEs; all other content is preserved. |
| 5 | `utilities\tests\pipelines\Get-ModuleList.Tests.ps1` | Add offline root-ownership, adoption, team, inheritance, invalid-metadata, stale-marker and filter regressions. |
| 6 | `utilities\tests\pipelines\ModuleReadMeNotices.Tests.ps1` | Add isolated README tests without the existing integration suite's checkout-based repair logic. |
| 7 | `utilities\tests\pipelines\MetadataWorkflow.Tests.ps1` | Guard against reintroducing ownership checks against marker files or lagging index handles. |

`Get-ModuleList -IsOrphaned` is explicitly an **offline ownership filter**, not a public catalog lifecycle-status query. It does not infer actual publication from local version files, or reinterpret deprecated/unpublished modules as catalog entries. `-Scope`, `-IsVersioned`, and `-HasChildren` remain independent. Full root validation reuses `Avm.Authoring` with `-SkipModuleVersionCheck`; this dependency is already installed by the CI environment action. The list operation neither installs dependencies nor accesses the public index.

This change does not modify module metadata, owners, versions, Bicep sources, compiled templates, workflow path exclusions, approval rules, issue-routing/tracking processes, or deprecation/movement notices relative to main. No module release is required. Related public guidance: [Azure/Azure-Verified-Modules#2964](https://github.com/Azure/Azure-Verified-Modules/pull/2964).

The unchanged upstream `CodeOwnersGovernance.Tests.ps1:40` has one pre-existing `PSUseSingularNouns` warning for `Get-TestCodeOwners`; not changed as part of this rebase. |

prs.author: abhisheksharma-ops
prs.body:
## Description

Updates all API versions in `avm/res/azure-stack-hci/cluster` to the latest supported versions, and implements resource-derived types for the `tags` parameters ([BCPNFR1](https://azure.github.io/Azure-Verified-Modules/spec/BCPNFR1)).

### API version updates

| Resource type | From | To |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Microsoft.AzureStackHCI/clusters` | `2025-10-01` | `2026-04-30` |
| `Microsoft.AzureStackHCI/clusters/deploymentSettings` | `2025-10-01` | `2026-04-30` |
| `Microsoft.AzureStackHCI/edgeDevices` | `2025-10-01` | `2026-04-30` |
| `Microsoft.HybridCompute/machines` | `2024-07-10` | `2026-07-15` |
| `Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults` | `2021-06-01-preview` | `2026-02-01` |
| `Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/secrets` (×5) | `2021-06-01-preview` | `2026-02-01` |
| `Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts` | `2023-01-01` | `2026-04-01` |
| `Microsoft.Resources/deployments` (AVM telemetry) | `2024-07-01` | `2025-04-01` |

Two resource types move off **preview** onto GA API versions (`Microsoft.KeyVault/*` and the Arc machine `reference()` calls).

The API versions embedded in `reference()` calls were also aligned with their corresponding resource declarations, since these are not validated at compile time:

| Call | From | To |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reference(hciNode, ...).identity.principalId` (×4) | `2023-10-03-preview` | `2026-07-15` |
| `reference(hciNode, ...).properties.displayName` | `2022-12-27` | `2026-07-15` |
| `reference(.../edgeDevices/default, ...).nicDetails` | `2024-01-01` | `2026-04-30` |

### Rationale for version selection

- **AzureStackHCI resources use `2026-04-30`, not the newest `2026-10-01`.** A schema diff of the two versions shows `2026-10-01` adds only read-only telemetry properties (`error`, `percentComplete`, `additionalData`, `recommendedSteps` on deployment/validation steps, plus `sdnProperties`). All writable properties and supporting type definitions are byte-identical between the two. Additionally, Bicep currently has **no type definitions** for `2026-10-01`, so adopting it would silently disable compile-time property validation (`BCP081`) for the cluster resources.
- **Key Vault and Storage target the newest versions present in AVM's `apiSpecsList.json`** (`2026-02-01` / `2026-04-01`) rather than the newest versions advertised by ARM (`2026-05-15` / `2026-06-01`), so the module stays clean against the AVM API-version compliance test.
- **`Microsoft.Resources/deploymentScripts` intentionally remains at `2023-08-01`.** ARM advertises `2026-04-01`, but there are no Bicep type definitions and no published swagger for it, which produces a `BCP081` warning on the resource that executes the entire cluster deployment, for no functional gain.

### BCPNFR1 — resource-derived types

The following parameters were changed from `object?` to resource-derived types, adding IntelliSense support and resolving the AVM complex-data-type warning:

| Parameter | New type |
| --- | --- |
| `tags` | `resourceInput<'Microsoft.AzureStackHCI/clusters@2026-04-30'>.tags?` |
| `azureStackLCMUserCredentialTags` | `resourceInput<'Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/secrets@2026-02-01'>.tags?` |
| `localAdminCredentialTags` | `resourceInput<'Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/secrets@2026-02-01'>.tags?` |
| `witnessStoragekeyTags` | `resourceInput<'Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/secrets@2026-02-01'>.tags?` |
| `defaultARBApplicationTags` | `resourceInput<'Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/secrets@2026-02-01'>.tags?` |

This is backwards compatible — passing an untyped `object` to these parameters still compiles.

### Validation

Beyond the standard static validation, this change was verified with a full two-phase deployment against a live 3-node Azure Local cluster:

- **Validate** phase: `Succeeded`, `validationStatus.status = Success`
- **Deploy** phase: `Succeeded`, `deploymentStatus.status = Success`
- Resulting cluster: `provisioningState = Succeeded`, `status = ConnectedRecently`, 3 nodes reporting, custom location and Arc Resource Bridge created

A post-deployment check of every changed resource type passed **33/33**, including:

- `reference(machines, '2026-07-15').properties.displayName` correctly resolving `physicalNodes[].name`
- `reference(edgeDevices, '2026-04-30').nicDetails` correctly resolving `physicalNodes[].ipv4Address`
- Role assignments bound to node identities, confirming `reference(hciNode, '2026-07-15').identity.principalId`
- `listKeys(..., '2026-04-01')` feeding the `WitnessStorageKey` secret
- Key Vault secrets created at `2026-02-01`, with the conditional `DefaultARBApplication` secret correctly omitted when no ARB service principal is supplied

These runtime checks matter because the API versions inside `reference()` and `listKeys()` are not type-checked by Bicep and would otherwise only surface as failures at deployment time.

Local compilation is clean: **0 errors, 0 warnings** (previously 8 `use-recent-api-versions` warnings).

### Backwards compatibility

No parameters or outputs were added, renamed, or removed. The module's external interface is unchanged. Module version bumped `0.5` → `0.6`.

### Related

Partial overlap with #7374 (draft), which makes the same `Microsoft.KeyVault` updates (`2021-06-01-preview` → `2026-02-01`) to this module's `modules/secrets.bicep` as part of a broader repository-wide Key Vault update. The changes are identical, so whichever merges second should rebase cleanly; this PR additionally covers the AzureStackHCI, HybridCompute, Storage, and telemetry API versions plus the BCPNFR1 work.

## Description

Fixes #7394

On `avm/res/azure-stack-hci/cluster`, when `Validate` and `Deploy` are run as **two separate module invocations** (the recommended Azure Local pattern — validate as a gate, then deploy), the portal cluster **Deployments** blade shows **"Validate input = Unknown"** even though **Deploy** is green and the cluster is healthy.

### Root cause

The inline cluster deployment script (`src/deploy.sh`) deleted the singleton `deploymentSettings/default` resource whenever a Deploy run found it left in **Validate** mode:

```
if [ "$DEPLOYMENT_MODE" = "Validate" ]; then
    echo "Removing stale Validate-mode resource..."
    az resource delete --ids ".../deploymentSettings/default"
```

Deleting and recreating the resource in Deploy-only mode discards the RP-reported `reportedProperties.validationStatus` written during Validate, so the portal "Validate input" tile has nothing to read → **Unknown**.

### Why the delete is avoidable (grounded)

The `Validate` → `Deploy` transition updates the **same** resource in place — no delete is required:

- **Azure Quickstart** [`create-cluster`](https://github.com/Azure/azure-quickstart-templates/tree/master/quickstarts/microsoft.azurestackhci/create-cluster) exposes a single `deploymentMode` parameter (`Validate` | `Deploy`, default `Validate`, *"First must pass Validate prior running Deploy"*) and **redeploys the same resource** with the mode changed — no delete step.
- **[ARM deployment modes (Microsoft Learn)](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-resource-manager/templates/deployment-modes):** the default Incremental mode **updates resources in place and deletes nothing** unless type/location changes or Complete mode is used.
- **This module's own nested loop** (`modules/deployment-setting.bicep`) already transitions `Validate` → `Deploy` on the same `default` singleton via two sequential deployments (`@batchSize(1)`, Validate first) with **no delete** — proving the in-place transition works.

### The change

In `src/deploy.sh`, a **succeeded** Validate resource is no longer deleted — the script redeploys `Deploy` over it in place, preserving `validationStatus`. A **non-succeeded/stale** Validate resource is still removed (clean-retry safeguard). `main.json` was regenerated via `Set-AVMModule`.

This is **cosmetic and preventive**: it does not repair already-deployed clusters (a `Deploy + Succeeded` singleton hits the script's idempotency skip), but it keeps both portal tiles green for future deployments.

### Testing

- `Set-AVMModule` regenerated `main.json` (script is inlined via `loadTextContent`); interface/README unchanged.
- `bicep lint main.bicep` — clean (exit 0); `bash -n src/deploy.sh` — clean.
- Static-validation Pester suite (`module.tests.ps1`) scoped to the module: **91 passed, 9 skipped (N/A features)**. The single failure is the pre-existing, repo-wide *"issue template alphabetical position"* check (lists only unrelated `avm/ptn/*` modules; not touched by this PR).
- No live end-to-end run: the target behavior is grounded in the sources above; an already-deployed cluster cannot exercise the changed path due to the idempotency skip.

### Validation evidence (exercised against a live Azure Local deployment)

The rewritten `src/deploy.sh` was run end-to-end against a real Azure Local (Azure Stack HCI) cluster resource to confirm the fix behaves as intended.

**1. Two-phase split is real.**
With `deploymentOperations` including `Validate`, the script issued the validation as its **own** `az deployment group create` (a dedicated `hci-deployment-validate-<epoch>` deployment), separate from the Deploy operation — matching the ARM quickstart's "Validate first, then Deploy" flow instead of fusing both into a single deployment.

**2. `validationStatus` is retained on the resource (the actual fix).**
After the Validate phase, querying the cluster's `deploymentSettings/default` returned a **non-empty** `reportedProperties.validationStatus`:

```
deploymentMode:  Validate
validationEmpty: false      # validationStatus is populated, not wiped
```

A populated `validationStatus` is exactly what keeps the portal **"Validate input"** tile from falling back to **Unknown**. Under the previous script, a Validate-mode resource was unconditionally deleted before Deploy, which erased this record and produced the Unknown tile.

**3. No delete of a succeeded Validate.**
The Deploy phase now deploys **in place** over the existing `default` resource; only a stale / non-succeeded Validate is removed. This preserves the validation record across the Validate → Deploy transition.

**Coverage.** All three `deploymentOperations` combinations — `['Validate']`, `['Deploy']`, and `['Validate','Deploy']` — follow the same in-place, no-wipe path, so both portal tiles stay populated. The module's public interface is unchanged (backward compatible), and existing idempotency semantics (`Deploy` + `Succeeded` ⇒ skip; `Deploy` + not-succeeded ⇒ fail) are preserved.

prs.author: a3burak
prs.body:
## Description

- Added the optional parameter `customerManagedKeyDbfsRoot` (`customerManagedKeyType`), which encrypts the workspace's DBFS root storage account with a customer-managed key through `properties.parameters.encryption`. Key Vault and Managed HSM keys are both supported, following the same pattern as `customerManagedKey` and `customerManagedKeyManagedDisk`.
- Added the output `storageAccountIdentityPrincipalId`, the identity of the DBFS root storage account that needs access to that key. It is available once `prepareEncryption` is enabled, matching how `managedDiskIdentityPrincipalId` is exposed for the managed disk key.
- Added the e2e test `cmk-dbfs`.

### Why

The module supports customer-managed keys for managed services and managed disks, but not for the third feature Azure Databricks offers, the DBFS root. A workspace that must use customer-managed keys for all data at rest, as PCI DSS and similar regimes expect, cannot be expressed through the module today.

The storage account identity is created by the provider when `prepareEncryption` is set, and it must hold `Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User` on the key before the key is applied. The module had that identity commented out as read only and did not output it, so a caller had no way to grant it without reading the resource back separately.

### How it is used

The key cannot be applied in the same deployment that first creates the identity, because the grant has to exist in between. The new test shows the sequence:

1. Deploy the workspace with `prepareEncryption: true`.
2. Grant `storageAccountIdentityPrincipalId` `Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User` on the key.
3. Deploy the workspace again with `customerManagedKeyDbfsRoot` (then an idempotency run).

Without `keyVersion` the storage account follows the latest key version. Verified outside this repository on a VNet-injected premium workspace: all three customer-managed key features enabled together, a redeploy that omits `parameters.encryption` leaves the DBFS root key in place (no write reaches the storage account), and jobs run normally afterwards.

### Compatibility

Additive. The parameter is optional and the encryption block is written through a conditional spread, so callers that do not set it produce the same request body as before. `parameters.encryption` exists at the module's current API version `2024-05-01`; the module builds free of BCP diagnostics.

### Relation to #7381

Independent of #7381 (API version `2026-01-01` and `computeMode`), and based on `main`. Both bump `version.json` to `0.13` and touch `CHANGELOG.md`, `README.md` and `main.json`, so whichever merges second needs a rebase and the next minor version. Happy to rebase this one onto #7381 instead if the reviewer prefers a single release.

## Description

Addresses the pre-deployment regional recovery gap exposed by the [BAMI Lab canary run](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/36429053903). This is a standalone change from `main`, not stacked on [#7405](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/7405). That review, its branch and its trigger label are unchanged.

### Behavior

- Query resource-provider metadata with an explicit namespace. [The cmdlet documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/az.resources/get-azresourceprovider) confirms that unqualified enumeration returns registered providers only. Missing metadata is no longer treated as global or sent to excluded WestEurope. The approved region list is unchanged.
- Before deployment, allow at most **three total validation attempts in distinct supported, allowed, nonexcluded regions**. Retry only wholly regional errors: `RequestDisallowedByAzure` with the `locationineligible` link, or narrowly classified regional capacity/availability errors. Mixed, malformed, unknown, permission, authentication, configuration and assertion errors stop.
- Restore pristine region-token inputs after each failed attempt. The successful candidate is used consistently in template parameters, referenced token files, the validation output and the subsequent deployment.
- Keep explicit custom, CI-parameter and token locations pinned; conflicting pins fail. Explicitly global resources retain their resource-group/metadata location. Resource-group-scope validation does not relocate or recreate a group to enable recovery.
- Keep deployment retries **outside** the regional-validation loop: deployment starts only after successful validation, and its existing maximum of three attempts stays in that validated region. There is no post-deployment regional failover, resource-deletion redesign, assertion retry, or change to retention/deployment-name cleanup. Cancellation stops further attempts.
- Document the contract in the composite-action descriptions and the directly related PowerShell help. Preserve subscription selection, authentication and secure CI-parameter handling.

The specific reason provider enumeration was empty in the historical canary is not asserted as proven. Offline fixtures reproduce the missing-registered-provider case and the observed regional validation error; no live provider lookup or canary rerun was performed.

## Pipeline Reference

| Pipeline |
| -------- |
| Local offline validation of `3feab0ae188000ffb1d11ace9d6ac5bd7eb68332`: **135 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** |
| PowerShell parsing and `Invoke-ScriptAnalyzer -Severity Error`: **8 files, zero errors** |
| `npm exec --offline --no -- prettier --check '.github\actions\templates\avm-validateModuleDeployment\action.yml'`: passed |
| `git diff HEAD^ HEAD --check`: passed |

Before/after evidence: the same selector regression fails against the original code because it returns `WestEurope` instead of an eligible region, and passes against this change. Runtime integration tests execute the actual action scripts and helpers with mocked Azure/network operations, including candidate/token propagation, bounded exhaustion, cancellation, cleanup failures and unchanged same-region deployment retry ownership.

Reproduce the focused suite from the repository root:

```powershell
Import-Module Pester -MinimumVersion 5.0
Import-Module powershell-yaml
$configuration = New-PesterConfiguration
$configuration.Run.Path = @(
    '.\utilities\tests\pipelines\Get-AvailableResourceLocation.Tests.ps1'
    '.\utilities\tests\pipelines\Test-TemplateDeploymentWithRetry.Tests.ps1'
    '.\utilities\tests\pipelines\RegionalValidationWorkflow.Tests.ps1'
    '.\utilities\tests\pipelines\CIParameterWorkflow.Tests.ps1'
    '.\utilities\tests\pipelines\TestSubscriptionWorkflow.Tests.ps1'
)
$configuration.Run.PassThru = $true
$configuration.Output.Verbosity = 'Normal'
$result = Invoke-Pester -Configuration $configuration
if ($result.FailedCount -gt 0 -or $result.FailedContainersCount -gt 0) {
    throw 'Regional retry regressions failed.'
}
```

**No Azure deployment or live setting change was performed. Do not add `PR: Run Checks` as part of this source-only review.** Live validation requires a separate decision; the failed canary has not been rerun.

## Summary

Source-only fixes for the Lab fixture incident documented in [#7405](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/7405) and [run 36482752869](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/36482752869). The initial `StorageAccountAlreadyTaken` failure is distinct from the later cleanup delay and credential-expiry symptoms. This change does not modify or claim to validate regional recovery.

- Give the max fixture's storage dependency a 16-character name derived from `uniqueString(resourceGroup.id, serviceShort)`. The subscription/resource-group/fixture scope determines the name, not the changing deployment-attempt name. Initial, repeat and retry deployments keep the same name. No public module API, version, resources, assertions or generated README changes.
- Retain every attempted `DeploymentNames` entry. Add optional `PreflightRejectedDeploymentNames` metadata only for a narrowly recognized, top-level Azure preflight rejection naming that exact submission. Nested `DeploymentFailed` errors, unknown/null submission results, context failures and cancellation are not evidence of preflight rejection.
- Pass that metadata through the existing composite action to cleanup. A marked attempt skips lookup retries only when the exact deployment query returns HTTP 404 with `DeploymentNotFound`. If a record exists, including a failed/partial deployment, it is still inspected and cleaned. Callers without metadata retain strict lookup behavior.
- Keep bounded discovery for required missing records: at most 40 discovery rounds, with the existing 60-second interval between rounds. Unclassified 404s, authentication, permission, transport and malformed-response failures remain explicit rather than becoming safe absence. Clean already discovered resources before reporting unresolved lookup failures, including failures in a later nested lookup. Zero discovered resources does not hide unresolved required names; a genuinely empty resolved deployment remains valid.
- Preserve the cleanup retention condition, deployment-name ownership and all four supported scopes. Submission/discovery cancellation propagates without retrying. Same-region deployment submissions remain outside the regional validation loop and are capped at three. No post-deployment regional failover or authentication-refresh framework is introduced.

## Offline validation

Tested source/remote head: [`456484cc61016851d40a2cfbd3f788b9c7b57679`](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/commit/456484cc61016851d40a2cfbd3f788b9c7b57679).

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Focused Pester run across 10 suites | **294 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** |
| New naming tests | Actual Bicep parameter evaluation reproduces the old cross-subscription collision, distinguishes five test scopes, proves initial/repeat/retry stability and checks lowercase alphanumeric 3..24-character output constraints |

## Description

Add an isolated, **manual-only** Bicep README drift preview. The new helper compares the 574 source-backed READMEs using `Invoke-AvmDocs -CheckDrift -IncludeRenderedContent`, preserves three source-less READMEs by exact path, byte length, and SHA-256, and permits only the eight pinned historical Key Vault comment lines. All other drift, rendering errors, missing paths, or coverage mismatches fail closed.

For changed `main.bicep`/`main.json`, compile all source-backed Bicep sources in the affected top-level module, including nested `/modules` children, using the tool-managed checksum-pinned Bicep CLI in the disposable checkout. Validate against the freshly compiled JSON and fail if checked-in `main.json` was stale. README-only and template/config-only checks use the existing committed compiled JSON, avoiding historical compiler-version churn. Root `bicepconfig.json` and tracked `docs/templates/avm-readme-v1.scriban` each select the full 574-source-backed set.

The workflow has **only `workflow_dispatch`** and `contents: read`: no automatic pull-request or push trigger, Azure authentication, OIDC, deployment, publishing, or release tags. The existing `Set-AVMModule`, module Pester/composite validation, deployment matrix, preview workflow, and README push exclusions are unchanged. This workflow was not dispatched.

Dependencies: the source checkout and HEAD verification are pinned to immutable commit `4962cd619347e2c111e50a3db0ae591081092ecd` in [Azure/azure-verified-modules-tools#195](https://github.com/Azure/azure-verified-modules-tools/pull/195). The separate assets are in [Azure/bicep-registry-modules#7416](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/7416). The completed frozen27 577-path comparator diagnostic did **not** overlay the assets or this wiring; the diagnostic is not an end-to-end validation of this helper or workflow. No further full rerun is requested today. Do not enable automatic checks or live CI cutover in this change.

## Focused published-blob integration (blocked)

A disposable checkout of this exact head `c87647608c85d1477945eeb9d73ff69106132e90` contains all 55 files byte-matched to the published asset head `36e9641e5ee04bde8a38faf234b848b49eea4530`: root `bicepconfig.json`, `docs/templates/avm-readme-v1.scriban` (SHA-256 `3099E02E1DB7B637F0ABA462E2213C9225DC9769C7000E8CF741F440695DAF34`), and 53 Notes. The imported authoring source checkout HEAD is the approved `4962cd619347e2c111e50a3db0ae591081092ecd`, manifest SHA-256 `2B6ECA01F8852829EB5351591A0C384309CB6DCA2C56E05D901430D24B56EE66`; the tool-managed Bicep CLI reports `0.47.16`.

## Description

Updates the Azure Stack HCI resources in `avm/res/azure-stack-hci/cluster` from `2026-04-30` to the GA API version `2026-10-01`.

| Resource type | From | To |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Microsoft.AzureStackHCI/clusters` | `2026-04-30` | `2026-10-01` |
| `Microsoft.AzureStackHCI/clusters/deploymentSettings` | `2026-04-30` | `2026-10-01` |
| `Microsoft.AzureStackHCI/edgeDevices` | `2026-04-30` | `2026-10-01` |

This covers every place these versions are used: the resource declarations, the `existing` cluster in the `deployment-setting` child module, the `reference(.../edgeDevices/default, ...)` call that resolves `physicalNodes[].ipv4Address`, and the resource-derived type of the `tags` parameter. No other API versions change.

`version.json` is already `0.6` (from #7384) and `0.6.0` has not been published yet (latest is `0.5.0`), so the change is folded into the existing `0.6.0` entry in `CHANGELOG.md`.

### Schema impact: no parameter changes

A diff of the PUT body schemas of the three resource types between the [`2026-04-30`](https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/blob/9bf19532443271e5c02c7968bea48ba632b749ad/specification/azurestackhci/resource-manager/Microsoft.AzureStackHCI/StackHCI/stable/2026-04-30/hci.json) and [`2026-10-01`](https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/blob/9bf19532443271e5c02c7968bea48ba632b749ad/specification/azurestackhci/resource-manager/Microsoft.AzureStackHCI/StackHCI/stable/2026-10-01/hci.json) specifications (added in Azure/azure-rest-api-specs#44812), resolving `$ref`, `allOf` and the `kind` discriminator, shows:

| Resource type | Writable changes | Read-only additions | Removed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clusters` | None | `sdnProperties` | None |
| `clusters/deploymentSettings` | `eceSecretName` gains `chapCredential` and `mutualChapCredential` | `percentComplete`, `error`, `additionalData`, `recommendedSteps` on validation and deployment steps | None |
| `edgeDevices` | None | `reportedProperties.networkProfile.sdnProperties` | None |

- The two new `eceSecretName` values are documented as "iSCSI CHAP authentication during edge machine node preparation". They belong to the new `edgeMachines` resource types in `2026-10-01`, not to the Arc machine and edge device flow this module uses, and the enum is extensible (`modelAsString: true`).
- All 70 property paths the module sets or reads exist unchanged in `2026-10-01`. The values the module restricts with `@allowed` (`deploymentMode`, `operationType`, storage `configurationMode`) are unchanged.
- No parameters or outputs are added, renamed, or removed.

### Why move to `2026-10-01` now

#7384 kept these resources on `2026-04-30` because Bicep has no type definitions for `2026-10-01`, which disables compile-time property validation for them. That is still the case in Bicep `0.47.16`. This PR adopts the GA version anyway, and closes that gap with the schema diff above and an end-to-end deployment on a live cluster (below).

Until a Bicep release includes the `2026-10-01` types, the build reports 5 non-blocking warnings (`main` currently has none). They go away without code changes once the types ship:

- `BCP081` (×4): no types available for `clusters`, `edgeDevices` and `clusters/deploymentSettings` at `2026-10-01`.
- `BCP321` (×1): `tags: tags` on the cluster resource, a side effect of the missing types.

The AVM API-version test will also warn, because AVM's `apiSpecsList.json` does not list `2026-10-01` yet. That test is warning-only.

### Validation

- `Set-AVMModule` regenerated `main.json` and the READMEs; running it again produces no changes.
- Static validation (`module.tests.ps1`) for this module: 92 passed, 0 failed.
- Validated end-to-end with a successful Validate and Deploy run on an Azure Local cluster.

### Related

- #7395 also changes this module's `CHANGELOG.md` and `main.json`. Whichever merges second needs a rebase and a fresh `Set-AVMModule` run.

## Description

# Static Site Private DNS Deployment Issue

## Initial Issue

The deployment failed with the following errors:

`Warning BCP318:
The value of type "module | null" may be null at the start of the deployment.`
`Error InvalidTemplate:
The template resource '...-staticSite-PrivateEndpoint-0' reference to
'...-staticSite-PrivateDnsZone' requires an API version.`

The affected code in modules/Microsoft.Web/static-site/main.bicep was:
`privateDnsZoneGroup: privateEndpoint.?privateDnsZoneGroup ?? {
  privateDnsZoneGroupConfigs: [
    {
      privateDnsZoneResourceId: staticSite_privateDnsZone.outputs.resourceId
    }
  ]
}`

### Root Cause
The staticSite_privateDnsZone module is deployed conditionally:
`createPrivateDnsZone == 'Enabled'`

When createPrivateDnsZone is set to Disabled, the module is not deployed. However, the fallback expression in the ?? operator still contains a reference to the module:
`staticSite_privateDnsZone.outputs.resourceId`

The Bicep ?? operator is compiled to the ARM coalesce() function. ARM can evaluate the fallback expression even when an existing privateDnsZoneGroup has already been supplied.

As a result, ARM attempts to resolve a reference to a module that was not deployed. Since the reference does not contain a resolvable API version, the deployment fails with the InvalidTemplate error.

The same reference also causes warning BCP318, because the conditional module can be null.

### Solution
The module reference must be placed inside a conditional expression:
`privateDnsZoneGroup: privateEndpoint.?privateDnsZoneGroup ?? (createPrivateDnsZone == 'Enabled'
  ? {
      privateDnsZoneGroupConfigs: [
        {
          privateDnsZoneResourceId: staticSite_privateDnsZone!.outputs.resourceId
        }
      ]
    }
  : null)`

The expression now behaves as follows:

If privateEndpoint.privateDnsZoneGroup is provided, that configuration is used.
If no DNS zone group is provided and createPrivateDnsZone is Enabled, the resource ID of the newly created DNS zone is used.
If no DNS zone group is provided and createPrivateDnsZone is Disabled, the value is set to null.

## Description

Source-only fix for request timeouts bypassing deployment cleanup. The original [workflow run](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/36690626584/attempts/1) and [IP Group defaults job](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/36690626584/job/109807448282) remain failed: the deployment command timed out and normal cleanup was skipped. An independently completed ARM deployment is not treated as a successful CI run.

The submission and discovery paths previously treated every `OperationCanceledException`, including `TaskCanceledException` with a typed `TimeoutException`, as cancellation. Submission could therefore escape before the composite action wrote its cleanup outputs; discovery could discard already identified resources.

- Distinguish typed request/deadline timeouts from genuine cancellation through inner exceptions, PowerShell error-record wrappers, and aggregate errors. Unclassified cancellation and `PipelineStoppedException` still stop further work; timeout wording alone does not override cancellation.
- Keep timeouts and unknown, missing, or nonterminal submission results explicitly failed, without another deployment submission. Preserve every actually attempted name and prior preflight-rejection metadata. Failures before submission do not create fictitious cleanup names. Confirmed failed results, the exact Az `DeploymentFailed` message for the attempted deployment, and confirmed preflight rejections retain the existing maximum of three same-region attempts.
- Emit deployment-name arrays before the action reports failure, leaving the output empty when nothing was submitted. Keep the existing cleanup, cancellation, and resource-retention condition unchanged.
- Retain known cleanup targets when discovery times out and report the lookup failure after scoped removal. A timeout cannot be accepted as `DeploymentNotFound`, even if an error record carries that ID. Empty exception messages no longer initiate an unguarded diagnostic lookup that could lose ownership metadata.

**Offline validation:** 326 tests passed, zero failed or skipped, on commit `abb8fd8c9771ac4312185d0b5c4341dfc41c8098` (base `695f0a85419c8521206b461e914bf5c54fcfddf8`), using PowerShell 7.6.6 and Pester 5.7.1. The existing baseline passed 64 cleanup/regional tests; the first added regression set reproduced 26 failures before the source fix.

The passing suites are `DeploymentCleanupWorkflow`, `RegionalValidationWorkflow`, `Test-TemplateDeploymentWithRetry`, `Get-AvailableResourceLocation`, `CIParameterWorkflow`, `Get-CIParameterMap`, `Get-TestSubscriptionList`, `TestSubscriptionWorkflow`, and `Get-OrderedResourcesList`. Coverage executes the actual composite-action scripts and cleanup condition with mocked Azure boundaries, including typed timeout wrappers after acceptance, earlier partial attempts, all four scopes, strict absence handling, discovery failures, secure-input redaction, retention, and a real stopped PowerShell runspace. Changed PowerShell ranges pass formatting; parsing and PSScriptAnalyzer introduce no errors or new warnings.

**Scope and limits:** No live Azure/Entra calls or jobs, auth refresh, timeout increases, execution labels, module fixtures, APIs, versions, tenant selectors, permissions, or publication behavior were changed. No recovery-to-success or background retry mechanism was added. The original log does not establish its exception-type chain; the offline regressions exercise the relevant typed .NET shapes. Live qualification remains intentionally unperformed, and this source is held as a draft.

## Pipeline Reference

| [Original failing workflow, attempt 1](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/36690626584/attempts/1) — historical evidence only; not rerun or counted as green. |

## Description

Updates `avm/res/hybrid-compute/machine` and its published `extension` child module to the newest stable HybridCompute API version, `2026-07-15`.

| Module | Resource type | From | To | Version |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `hybrid-compute/machine` | `Microsoft.HybridCompute/machines` | `2025-01-13` | `2026-07-15` | `0.6.0` |
| `hybrid-compute/machine/extension` | `Microsoft.HybridCompute/machines/extensions` (and the referenced parent `machines`) | `2025-01-13` | `2026-07-15` | `0.2.0` |

The other resource types in the module are already on their newest stable API versions (`Microsoft.GuestConfiguration/guestConfigurationAssignments` `2024-04-05`, `Microsoft.Authorization/locks` `2020-05-01`, `Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments` `2022-04-01`).

### Schema impact: no parameter changes

A diff of the PUT body schemas between the [`2025-01-13`](https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/blob/85efeb3571600039a5ab10b03ea217f637c4720e/specification/hybridcompute/resource-manager/Microsoft.HybridCompute/HybridCompute/stable/2025-01-13/HybridCompute.json) and [`2026-07-15`](https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/blob/85efeb3571600039a5ab10b03ea217f637c4720e/specification/hybridcompute/resource-manager/Microsoft.HybridCompute/HybridCompute/stable/2026-07-15/openapi.json) specifications shows:

| Resource type | Writable additions | Read-only additions | Removed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `machines` | `identity.userAssignedIdentities`, `properties.hardwareResourceId` | `properties.statusReason`, `clientId` / `principalId` of user-assigned identities | None |
| `machines/extensions` | None | None | None |

- Every property path the two modules set or read exists unchanged in `2026-07-15`, so no parameters or outputs are added, renamed, or removed. The new optional properties are not exposed by this change.
- `identity.type` gains `UserAssigned` values; the module keeps using `SystemAssigned`.
- `vmId` is now documented as a `uuid`, and `parentClusterResourceId` and `privateLinkScopeResourceId` as ARM IDs. The module's empty-string defaults for these are still accepted: the service generates the `vmId`.

### Versioning

Both modules get a MINOR bump, as the module's previous API version update (`2024-07-10` → `2025-01-13`) did with `0.5.0`: `machine` `0.5` → `0.6` and `extension` `0.1` → `0.2`, with matching `CHANGELOG.md` entries.

### Validation

- `Set-AVMModule -Recurse` regenerated `main.json` and the READMEs; running it again produces no changes.
- Static validation (`module.tests.ps1`) for the module and its `extension` child: 155 passed, 0 failed. Bicep types are available for `2026-07-15` (no compile warnings), and AVM's API version list includes it.
- Validated end-to-end with a successful deployment of an `HCI` Arc machine using the module defaults in an Azure Local environment, and a re-deployment that changed nothing. The `extension` child module is validated statically; deploying it requires an Arc machine with a connected agent.

### Related

`avm/res/azure-stack-hci/virtual-machine-instance` consumes this module (currently `0.4.1`); it will be updated in a separate PR once `0.6.0` is published.

## Description

Fixes the failed publishing of `avm/res/azure-stack-hci/virtual-machine-instance` `0.2.0` after #7429.

The module pipeline on `main` ([run 36736704112](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/36736704112)) failed the static test *"Set-ModuleReadMe script should not apply any updates"*, so `0.2.0` was not published. The README's "Cross-referenced modules" section still listed `br/public:avm/res/hybrid-compute/machine:0.4.1`, while `main.bicep` references `0.6.0` since #7429. The README had been generated with a stale local cross-reference cache: the README tooling caches cross-references in a temporary file for up to a day.

This PR regenerates the README with a fresh cache. The only change is that line, `0.4.1` → `0.6.0`. There are no module code changes: `version.json` stays `0.2`, and `0.2.0` remains the unpublished target version with its existing `CHANGELOG.md` entry.

### Validation

- `Set-AVMModule` with fresh caches produces no further changes.
- The module workflow ran on this branch with static validation only ([run 36740648686](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/36740648686)): all static tests, including *"Set-ModuleReadMe script should not apply any updates"*, and all PSRule checks passed.

### After merge

The module workflow's `push` trigger ignores `README.md` changes, so merging this PR does not start the pipeline. To publish `0.2.0`, the `avm.res.azure-stack-hci.virtual-machine-instance` workflow needs to be run manually on `main` after the merge.

+# Module Check and Publish Workflow
+
+The `.Module - Check and Publish` workflow provides a generic way to validate and publish one or more AVM modules. It is implemented by [`avm.module.yml`](./avm.module.yml).
+
+## Automatic checks
+
+Pushes to `main` that change files under `avm/`, excluding module `README.md` files, automatically:
+
+1. Discover the affected top-level modules.
+1. Run static, PSRule, and deployment validation.
+1. Calculate and log the release tags that would be created.
+
+Automatic runs cannot create tags. The preview path has read-only repository permissions and invokes the release logic with `WhatIf`.

+# Function App Pattern `[App/FunctionApp]`
+
+Deploys an Azure Function App together with its supporting resources: an App Service Plan, a Storage Account for the Function runtime, an Application Insights component, a Log Analytics workspace, and a User-Assigned Managed Identity used for runtime storage access and Application Insights ingestion. Secure defaults are always applied (HTTPS-only, TLS 1.2 minimum, FTP/FTPS deployment disabled, no anonymous blob access, and identity-based runtime storage access wherever the selected plan family supports it).

+

+
+1. **Provided SSH Key**: If you provide an SSH public key via the `sshPublicKey` parameter, it will be used consistently
+2. **Generated SSH Key**: If no SSH key is provided, the template will generate one and reuse the same key on subsequent deployments
+3. **No Changes on Re-deployment**: Running the same deployment multiple times will not change the SSH configuration
+
+**How it works:**
+- The PowerShell script checks if an SSH key resource already exists and reuses it
+- No `forceUpdateTag` is used, ensuring the deployment script doesn't run unnecessarily

+
+The use of Routing Intent in a Virtual Hub requires the hub be made 'secure' by associating a firewall (to serve as the next-hop for the routing policy).
+
+The 'azureFirewall' parameter in Microsoft.Network/virtualHubs is *read-only*; in order to properly deploy a Virtual Hub using Routing Intent, the hub's Resource ID must first be passed to the firewall in order for it to be properly associated. In order for this resource to work properly, the resources need to be created in the following order:
+
+- **Virtual Hub**: Suggest minimal hub configuration; name/location/addressPrefix/virtualWan.id
+- **Firewall**: Including Virtual Hub Resource ID in the firewall configuration
+- **Virtual Hub**: Including all remaining parameters + Routing Intent
+
